class.name: NetwQuantize
class.brief_description: The base a game extends to give one value type its own bit packer, and the type every quantizer slot is declared as.
class.description:
A quantizer turns a value into a fixed number of bits and back, trading precision for size. One is assigned per property through [method NetwMemberConfig.quantize], and the same resource may be shared by as many properties as want it. One quantizer handles [Vector2], [float] and [int] without nesting, because it is told the type. A quantizer turns a value into codes and never touches a stream itself. [method _stride] says how many codes one value spends, [method _bit_width] says how wide each of them is, [method _encode] returns one code per element, and [method _decode] rebuilds the value from all of them. The session writes those codes into its own packed row through [NetwBitStream], so a quantizer allocates nothing and a script override runs once per element rather than once per write. Each behaviour has two spellings. A subclass overrides [method _encode], [method _decode], [method _stride], [method _supports_type], [method _bit_width] and [method _max_error]. Every caller uses [method encode], [method decode], [method stride], [method supports_type], [method bit_width] and [method max_error] instead, because an override point reaches a GDScript override only and would find nothing on a quantizer written in C++. One written in C++ overrides the plain method, so no script is entered for it at all. [codeblock] # Assigned on a synchronizer's codec/<prop> slot, or in code: Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").quantize(NetwQuantizeScalar.new()) [/codeblock] Widths come from this resource on both peers, never the wire, so the decoder reconstructs the exact layout the encoder wrote. This base is abstract: a subclass ([NetwQuantizeScalar], [NetwQuantizeAngle], [NetwQuantizeQuaternion], [NetwQuantizeTransform2D], [NetwQuantizeTransform3D]) supplies the actual layout, and a game supplies its own by overriding the six virtuals. [codeblock] extends NetwQuantize
func _supports_type(type: int) -> bool: return type == TYPE_VECTOR2
func _bit_width(_type: int) -> int: return 10
func _stride(_type: int) -> int: return 2
func _encode(value: Variant, element: int) -> int: return roundi((value as Vector2)[element]) & 0x3ff
func _decode(codes: PackedInt64Array, _type: int) -> Variant: return Vector2(float(codes[0]), float(codes[1])) [/codeblock]

method.name: _bit_width
method.description: Returns the width of ONE code for a value of [param type], not the total. The total is [method total_bits], which is this times [method _stride]. Reached through [method bit_width].

method.name: _decode
method.description: Returns the value of [param type] that [param codes] stands for, inverting [method _encode]. [param codes] holds exactly [method _stride] entries, in element order. Reached through [method decode].

method.name: _encode
method.description: Returns the code for element [param element] of [param value], which must fit in [method _bit_width] bits. A row that meets a wider code rejects the whole row rather than truncating it. Reached through [method encode].

method.name: _max_error
method.description: Returns the worst-case round-trip error for a value of [param type]. Reached through [method max_error]. For a [Vector2] this is the error magnitude with both axes at their bound, so it compares directly against a reconciliation deadzone ([member NetwPredictionHandle.divergence_epsilon]). A correction threshold below this value triggers on quantization noise alone.

method.name: _stride
method.description: Returns how many codes one value of [param type] spends. A scalar spends one, a [Vector2] two. A layout whose parts do not share one width packs them into a single code instead, the way [NetwQuantizeQuaternion] does. Reached through [method stride].

method.name: _supports_type
method.description: Returns whether this quantizer can encode a value of [param type]. Reached through [method supports_type].

method.name: bit_width
method.description: Returns the width of ONE code for a value of [param type]. [method total_bits] is what a whole value costs.

method.name: decode
method.description: Returns the value of [param type] that [param codes] stands for, inverting [method encode].

method.name: encode
method.description: Returns the code for element [param element] of [param value].

method.name: is_same_layout
method.description: Returns whether [param other] encodes the identical bit layout: the same quantizer class and script with the same stored parameters. Two layout-equal quantizers read each other's bits, so a configuration re-declared per instance with fresh but identical quantizers is the same schema, not a conflict. [method NetwMemberConfig.quantize] warns only when a re-declaration fails this check.

method.name: max_error
method.description: Returns the worst-case round-trip error for a value of [param type].

method.name: stride
method.description: Returns how many codes one value of [param type] spends.

method.name: supports_type
method.description: Returns whether this quantizer can encode a value of [param type]. Callers that quantize opportunistically (entity RPC arguments) ask this before handing a value to [method encode], so the set of encodable types stays owned by each quantizer instead of duplicated at the call site.

method.name: total_bits
method.description: Returns what a whole value of [param type] costs, which is [method bit_width] times [method stride].
